title: Steak and Peppercorn Sauce Pasta
summary: Butter-basted steak sliced over pasta cooked in beef stock and tossed in a creamy black-pepper Parmesan sauce.
profile: Rich and savory: beefy umami from pasta cooked in bouillon-seasoned water, cream and Parmesan for fat and salt, and a forward but not harsh heat from 1–2 teaspoons of freshly cracked black pepper, with thyme and garlic butter perfuming the steak. The steak should have a deep brown crust and a pink, juicy medium-rare center (125–130°F / 52–54°C at the pull), and the sauce should be glossy and just thick enough to cling to every strand without pooling or turning gluey. Makes 2 servings in about 50 minutes, including a 30-minute rest for the steak out of the fridge (about 25 minutes hands-on); serve straight from the pan, with a green salad if you like. Best eaten fresh; keeps 2–3 days refrigerated (store the steak separately), and the cream sauce doesn't freeze well. Reheat the pasta in a skillet over low heat with a splash of water, and warm the steak slices briefly on top or eat them cold.

ingredients.note: a tender searing cut such as ribeye, strip or sirloin
table salt; to taste, for the steak and the sauce
or enough to coat the pan
from the bouillon pot, plus a splash more as needed

steps.text: Take the steak out of the fridge about 30 minutes before cooking. Pat it dry and season generously on both sides with salt and the ground black pepper.
steps.tip: A dry, less-cold surface browns faster, so the crust forms before the center overcooks.

steps.text: Meanwhile, bring the water to a boil in a medium saucepan and whisk in the Better Than Bouillon (with another concentrate, follow its package ratio for 4 cups). No extra salt needed.
steps.tip: Cooking the pasta in beef stock seasons it from the inside and makes the reserved water a ready-made sauce base.

steps.text: Cook the pasta until about 2 minutes shy of al dente (check the package time). Scoop out at least 1 cup of the cooking liquid, then drain.
steps.tip: It finishes cooking in the sauce, so it absorbs flavor instead of going soft.

steps.text: Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. When it shimmers, sear the steak about 2 minutes per side for medium-rare, until deeply browned and it reads 125–130°F (52–54°C) in the thickest part (medium: pull at 135°F / 57°C).
steps.tip: Two minutes a side suits a ¾-inch steak; a 1-inch-plus steak needs 3–4 minutes per side, so trust the thermometer.

steps.text: In the final minute, lower the heat to medium and add the butter, thyme and sliced garlic. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming butter over the steak until fragrant, about 1 minute.
steps.tip: Lowering the heat first keeps the butter browning, not burning.

steps.text: Move the steak, thyme and sliced garlic to a board and let the steak rest at least 5 minutes while you make the sauce. Keep the fat in the pan.
steps.tip: Resting lets the juices settle so they stay in the meat when you slice.

steps.text: In the same pan over medium heat, sauté the onion and minced garlic until soft and fragrant, 2–3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.

Pour in the heavy cream and the reserved pasta water. Stir in the Parmesan and the freshly cracked black pepper and simmer gently until slightly thickened and it coats a spoon, 2–3 minutes. Taste and add salt only if needed.
steps.tip: The bouillon water and Parmesan are already salty, so season last.

steps.text: Add the pasta and toss over medium heat until silky and glossy, 1–2 minutes, adding a splash more pasta water if it tightens.
steps.tip: The starch in the pasta water is what emulsifies the cream and cheese into a clinging sauce.

steps.text: Slice the steak against the grain and serve it over the pasta, with any resting juices poured on top and the parsley scattered over.

changelog.summary: Built from foodierandy.com (schema.org recipe). Fixes: moved the 30-minute steak tempering to the start and counted it in the total time; added a medium-rare pull temperature, since the source gave only 2 minutes per side; added timers for the rest and the sauce simmer (source said only "while you make the sauce" / "until slightly thickened"); merged the two salt lines into one; dropped the gram/ml notes that wouldn't scale.
